source: If you listen to pop music, you’ve likely heard BeatBox 2 (feat. Pooh Shiesty) by SpotemGottem, the most popular song in North Charleston.
claim: BeatBox 2 (feat. Pooh Shiesty) by SpotemGottem is the most popular song in North Charleston, with 14,600 YouTube views.

source: But head over to Charleston, and good 4 u by Olivia Rodrigo has BeatBox 2 (feat. Pooh Shiesty)-level popularity.
claim: Charleston is the nearest city to North Charleston with a different #1 song, and Charleston’s #1 song is good 4 u by Olivia Rodrigo.

source: Generally, cities in the area around North Charleston have different #1 songs, a sort of pop music melting pot.
claim: Around North Charleston, US cities have 3 different #1 songs: MONTERO (Call Me By Your Name) by Lil Nas X, BeatBox 2 (feat. Pooh Shiesty) by SpotemGottem, and good 4 u by Olivia Rodrigo.

source: The #1 hit in a particular region reflects the broader cultural edges of the USA’s geography, which has 5 different #1 songs.
claim: In the US, five #1 songs are the most widespread: good 4 u by Olivia Rodrigo (236 cities, 30.9%), Butter by BTS (217, 28.4%), RAPSTAR by Polo G (71, 9.3%), MONTERO (Call Me By Your Name) by Lil Nas X (67, 8.8%), and Outside (Better Days) by MO3, Og Bobby Billions (43, 5.6%).

source: If you listen to pop music, you’ve likely heard RAPSTAR by Polo G, the most popular song in Columbus.
claim: RAPSTAR by Polo G is the most popular song in Columbus, with 200,000 YouTube views.

source: The top song often changes when crossing international borders. 367 km away from Columbus is London, Canada, where “Body (Remix)” by Tion Wayne, Russ is a number one hit.
claim: London is 367 km from Columbus, and London’s #1 song is Body (Remix) by Tion Wayne, Russ.
code: (lambda d,g,x: d.assign(origin=g.geo_name, dist=2*6371*np.arcsin(np.sqrt(np.sin(np.radians(d.latitude-g.latitude)/2)**2 + np.cos(np.radians(g.latitude))*np.cos(np.radians(d.latitude))*np.sin(np.radians(d.longitude-g.longitude)/2)**2))).query('country_code != @g.country_code and track_link != @g.track_link and track_link not in @x').nsmallest(1,'dist')[['origin','geo_name','track_name','artist_name','dist']])(c, c[c.geo_name.eq('Columbus')].nlargest(1,'views').iloc[0], c[c.country_code.eq('US')].track_link.value_counts().pipe(lambda s: s[(s > 4) & (s/len(c[c.country_code.eq('US')]) > 0.04)].index))
